why:
The verifier brief is fine on item 1. Check 1 passes only on `BAD {}` and fails on `THREW` or any other result. Checking stderr for the file name appears only under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)", so it is not a PASS or FAIL condition.

The builder brief breaks item 2. Step 2 says to "write one line to stderr (e.g. `console.error`) that names the path and the parse error message" inside the catch. Step 4 then has the README describe it ("plus the warning if you added one"). That tells the builder to do more on a parse error than return {}. It is the same file-name or warning extra that the must_not list rules out. The step is marked optional and keeps the {} return, but the brief still invites the extra behaviour. So the briefs do not avoid everything on the must_not list.
